#3660. GDQ releases schedule for Awesome Games Done Quick 2027 in January, featuring new runs like Queen's Domain, Big Walk, Galactic Racer, and the incongruously not-new Yakuza 5

Following the full game list for Awesome Games Done Quick being released a little while ago, GDQ have now published the full schedule for the event running for a week from January 3rd through January 10th in Atlanta (and streamed on Twitch, of course). Included amongst the new games this year are 2026 releases like Queen's Domain, Star Wars: Galactic Racer, the Ocarina of Time remake, and Castlevania: Belmont's Curse, which all make a lot of sense as games practically made for speedrunning. Belmont's Curse, specifically, is set to be the event's final bonus game, only to be played if donation incentives are met (which I'm sure they will be, it's a Castlevania game at GDQ).

But then, there's also Big Walk, which I'm fascinated by the prospect of trying to speedrun as a group. It's listed as a '12 player showcase', which I can only imagine denotes it as more of a fun experiment to put on a show, rather than a world-record aiming speedrun. The chaos of twelve people trying to work together in Big Walk live on the GDQ stage is a spectacle that has my interest, either way. Also making the cut is train-flipping stunt game Denshattack!, which I simply have to mention got a resounding "✨🚂DENSHATTACK MENTIONED🚂✨" from James in the RPS chat this morning. I can't help but share his excitement, in fairness, since Denshattack! is just that cool.

As for some of the more out-there picks, which I say entirely positively, there's a run of not the DmC reboot, but specifically its bonus Vergil DLC, which is the first time I've heard that mentioned in years. Metroid Prime Origins, a fangame that 'demakes' the famously first-person Metroid Prime into a 2D sidescroller more akin to Zero Mission, is also on the cards; lovely to think there'll be a new speedrun for a new Metroid game just a month before Ravenous comes out. And finally, on a personal note because of my own biases, I'm deeply interested to see the Any% run of Yakuza 5 play out; that game is infamous for its ridiculous scope and length, so watching a runner try to get it down to only its most essential parts should be a treat. The schedule estimates around 2 hours for the run, to which I can only say good luck.

It's GTA 6's world, and we're just living in it. Rockstar's latest release is an astonishing technical achievement to behold, confounding even developers working on big-budget games like Naughty Dog's Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet. It's been 13 long years since GTA 5, but seeing the staggering advancements in visual detail, depth of interactivity, and overall scale in GTA 6, you'd think it's been even longer. And yet, CD Projekt Red says we'll see a similar technical leap in The Witcher 4 compared to The Witcher 3, which came out in 2015.

During the Q&A portion of CDPR's latest earnings call, joint-studio CEO Michał Nowakowski fields a question about GTA 6 and whether The Witcher fans can expect a similar improvement from The Witcher 4. He says the team at CDPR "did look at [GTA 6]" and "did see the differences," and "we believe there's gonna be a comparable leap between Witcher 3 and Witcher 4."

"It's been 11 years, we are working on The Witcher 4 to make it significantly better looking and improved in terms of pretty much every possible facet of the game, so yes, you can expect us to make a much bigger jump between The Witcher 3 and The Witcher 4," says Nowakowski.

There aren't many (read: any) studios with GTA 6's budget, which of course is supplied by Rockstar parent company Take-Two Interactive, but CDPR definitely has the resources to craft huge, visually stunning worlds packed with detail and complex systems that rival today's most expansive AAA games. Cyberpunk 2077 is the most recent example, but even 11 years on, The Witcher 3 absolutely holds up to modern open-world standards.

We're still a couple of years out from The Witcher 4's estimated 2028 release, but there's every reason to believe it'll make The Witcher 3 look downright dated, even after its recent remaster. Whether it'll truly mark a leap comparable to what Rockstar managed from GTA 5 to GTA 6 is a very different question we'll have to wait to answer.

Ciri in The Witcher 4 is "far more hot-headed" than Geralt, CD Projekt Red lead says, and "you are much more deeply involved in the story through her personal perspective"

#3657. Action RPG Showa American Story seemingly delayed into 2027, with no comment on why from developer NEKCOM

Despite being announced back in 2022 with an initial release window of 2025, NEKCOM's action RPG Showa American Story has been set for a late 2026 release date for a while now. That seems to have changed, however, as the release date on its Steam page has slipped to 2027 without any sort of announcement as to why.

In conversation with Automaton last month, the game's director Xiangyu Luo stated that "The game's content is already completely finished, and we're now at the stage of polishing its overall quality." As such, it would seem that this delay is to give the game a little more breathing room for bug fixes and quality assurance work, rather than rushing a holiday release just to hit its stated release window.

Based on my own time with Showa American Story, taking a little more time to clean it up would be a welcome choice. When I played a demo at Gamescom 2026, I was a little stunned by how awful it felt to play. The protagonist was a blank slate designed to be pretty and nothing more, and the combat was mind-numbingly oversimplified, its challenge mainly derived from the need to wrestle with its janky controls and the noticeable delay between button presses and attacks. In that same interview, Luo notes an awareness of the game being compared to the Yakuza/Like a Dragon series in being a 'wacky' open-world action RPG, saying that he's "happy that players are making that association", as "it means they've recognised Showa American Story as a rich RPG with plenty of content to sink their teeth into." I can respect him taking the comparison in stride, but what I played seemed like a pale imitation of LAD that missed what makes that series more than it seems on the surface.

I can hope that this delay can result in improvements to the critiques the game has faced — Luo did mention that "we've heard many valuable comments regarding the feel of the controls and how the action is presented" — and that Showa American Story releases in a good state sometime in 2027.

#3656. God of War Laufey's Faye actor jumps from games to live-action, as Amazon casts Deborah Ann Woll in upcoming series

After appearing in both God of War Ragnarok and next year's God of War Laufey, Deborah Ann Woll is about to reprise her role as Faye in Amazon Prime Video's upcoming live-action series.

Variety reports that the God of War cast list is now welcoming a second actor pulled straight from Sony Santa Monica's video game series. Deborah Ann Woll first showed up in the games as Kratos' wife and Atreus' mother during God of War Ragnarok, but she's also about to enter the spotlight proper in God of War Laufey.

Amazon's God of War cast now includes Dave Bautista (Guardians of the Galaxy) as god killer Kratos, Callum Vinson (Chucky) as Atreus, Mandy Patinkin as Odin and Ólafur Darri Ólafsson as Thor. Alastair Duncan is also making the game-to-show jump by stepping back into the figurative shoes of chatty head Mimir.

Earlier in the year, the God of War show halted production when former Kratos actor Ryan Hurst suffered an on-set injury. Bautista soon took over the role and production began again in October - all of Hurst's scenes had to be reshot, of course.

There's no release date yet for the show, but it's said to follow the Norse era of the games which began in 2018's more serious and stern revamp. Amazon ordered a two-season run for the show, which apparently means both seasons will be filmed back-to-back.

Meanwhile, God of War Laufey was recently delayed from February 2027 to May 2027, giving the PS5 exclusive slightly more breathing room away from Fable, Persona 4 Revival and Tomb Raider: Legacy of Atlantis.

"We will make the most of each moment until then by putting in the finishing touches and pushing the game to its fullest potential," developer Sony Santa Monica said at the time. "On behalf of everyone on the team, we appreciate your patience and we'll be back to share more updates soon."

While the game puts Faye in the leading role as she battles with gods in a multi-mythological afterlife, the studio was quick to note that her journey isn't considered a side game. God of War Laufey will still connect to future games in the series and, yep, Kratos will eventually be back, too.

"Genuinely, I thought I was going to be much more offended by it, but one, I'm not on social media, so that helps, and two, I don't know, I feel totally unbothered," Woll said of the online trolls who were targeting Laufey after its reveal this summer. "Because I just know it's great. It's okay if it's not your cup of tea, but in no universe is it bad."

Four years ago (oh my god) strategy RPG Symphony of War: The Nephilim Saga rather impressed our reviewer Jon Bolding. He wrote that "novel tactical mechanics make this indie a contender for the best strategy RPG this year".

Well, buckle up, 2027, because Symphony of War 2 has broken cover with a promise to release next year, and it's coming courtesy of the strategy sommeliers at publisher Hooded Horse, which I take as a very good sign.

SOW2 looks set to continue the Fire-Emblem-ish framework of its predecessor, tasking you with recruiting a gaggle of heroes to wage war with (and possibly compose symphonies, who's to say?) in "a world filled with political intrigue, betrayal, and tense, large-scale tactical battles". Which is a lot like our world, really.

It all looks very nice indeed. In the announcement trailer, we get glimpses of its squad-based combat and anime cutscenes, and I am officially into both. The art is poppy and distinctive, at some point an age-of-sail warship transforms into some kind of German WW1 destroyer, and the overworld triggers the regions in my brain devoted to thinking about Heroes of Might and Magic. Check, check, and check.

"Anime cutscenes!?" I hear you cry. "That sounds like the kind of thing that bespeaks a dense tapestry of lore I'll need to get to grips with first!" Well, apparently not. I am informed by Symphony of War 2's Steam page that the devs have no expectation you know what a "Nephilim Saga" even is before you pick this game up. "Symphony of War 2 is a standalone experience set several generations after the events of the first game—it can be enjoyed without having played Symphony of War: The Nephilim Saga". The game's tale of a fallen empire trying to un-fall can be enjoyed single-serve.

Dedicated servers complicate the "without a multiplayer subscription" part

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

"The crossplay era for Terraria starts here," declares developer Re-Logic in a new Steam post announcing "Phase One" of the iconic sandbox adventure game's crossplay rollout.

Terraria's new-fangled crossplay, which allows players on different platforms to share multiplayer worlds and progress, comes with a few caveats, but it's a big step forward nonetheless.

"Starting today, for most people using the same Wi-Fi/wired network you will be able to play together with any device which has v1.4.6 Terraria, without a multiplayer subscription," Re-Logic explains. "Xbox, PlayStation, Switch, Android, Apple, PC, Mac; if you're on the same network, in most circumstances your games should be able [to] see each other in the Local section of the NEW multiplayer menu."

What about online multiplayer for distant players? That's the focus of the second phase of crossplay. "This first phase of Crossplay is all about making it easier to play together on the local network," the devs reiterate.

Additionally, options for joining dedicated PC servers are a little complicated. To join on PlayStation or Xbox, you will need an online subscription, as at that point you're going through Sony and Microsoft's infrastructure.

"Switch cannot connect to privately hosted dedicated servers, either Local or Online. This is due to security and safety restrictions required by Nintendo for the platform," Re-Logic adds.

"If you are running a dedicated server on one of the server hosting services, the IP or web address can be manually input with the + Add Server button at the bottom of the multiplayer menu. Just type in the details. This will add an entry to the Server section which will remember the details for future sessions."

The full 1.4.6 patch notes add a bit more color. For example, Steam players can now invite their friends directly in-game "without opening the overlay." The devs snuck in a few balance changes, too, with Heavy variants of Armored Skeletons (very important) having their health rebalanced for Expert and Master modes.

As Terraria sells over 70 million copies, devs are done with promising final updates and say they'll "continue beyond 1.4.6"

#3653. Hooded Horse's latest tactics RPG is a sequel to Symphony of War, one of 2022's undersung favourites

Symphony of War II: Dominion promises a "deeper, more ambitious strategy RPG"

Dancing Dragons Games and Hooded Horse have announced Symphony of War II: Dominion, the sequel to 2022's Symphony of War: The Nephilim Saga. Sin noted the original as pretty special for being "a good strategy game", highlighting the unique importance of taking care of each and every army member, rather than just benching the ones that are less effective and/or pretty to look at. The Nephilism Saga is also somewhat rare in being a turn-based tactics game made in RPG Maker, as seems to be the case with its sequel, which is expanding to include naval combat.

Symphony of War II: Dominion Announcement Trailer | Strategy RPG Watch on YouTube

Dominion's premise mirrors its predecessor in setting a band of heroes from a wide variety of classes, with units ranging from heavy knights and light archers to cannon-lighting artillery and even dragons the size of large dogs; I do have to wonder if an actual hooded horse is one of the units. Over 100 different classes are available, with the core of the game being swapping out these units to create the most effective squads of units for each turn-based battle. As before, it's not just a matter of recruiting soldiers and never thinking about them again until their turn arrives; a cared for army is a strong army (Sun Tzu said that, probably), and nurturing your army with new gear, individual perks and specialisation to make the squad work not only on their own, but as a collective.

Phil Hamilton, founder of Dancing Dragon Games, elaborated that "With Symphony of War: Dominion, we’re building on what players loved about the first game while taking the series in a direction we’ve wanted to explore for years. We’re delivering a deeper, more ambitious strategy RPG without sacrificing the feel and flow that made the original special." Symphony of War II: Dominion releases sometime next year, so for now, get thinking about how you'll best take care of your squads. To paraphrase Sun Tzu again, keeping them fed is always a good start.

#3650. Activision calls Banjo-Kazooie one of its "iconic gaming franchises," raising hopes for long-awaited new game

Banjo-Kazooie - the iconic Rare platformer starring an absent-minded bear and the sassy red bird he carries in a backpack - has been on hiatus for years, but a new Activision job listing has raised hopes for a new game.

In a LinkedIn post advertising a 'Product Manager, Emergent Franchises' role, the publisher wrote that it's "home to iconic gaming franchises including Call of Duty, Crash Bandicoot, Spyro the Dragon, and now… Halo, Age of Empires, Sea of Thieves, and Banjo Kazooie."

"Become part of the team working on building, growing, and shaping many of these franchises," the listing goes on. "As a Product Manager, you will serve as the publishing product lead for an upcoming premium console & PC title, driving the product from concept to launch."

If you're scratching your brain trying to remember when Activision took control of the beloved platformer, well, it happened during Xbox's last massive internal shakeup. Amid the mass layoffs and studio divestments, Xbox also made some drastic changes to its corporate structure - Halo, World's Edge and Rare were all slotted under Activision's supervision.

Rare's 40-year history includes almost too many notable games to list, but the internal rejig presumably put Activision in control of games like Conker, Viva Pinata and Killer Instinct, alongside the aforementioned pirate hit Sea of Thieves and Banjo-Kazooie.

The job post is by no means confirmation that a new Banjo-Kazooie game is in development, but it is the only series named here that can be considered dormant, perhaps hinting that Activision has plans to revive it down the line. Crash Bandicoot 4 and Spyro: A Realm Beyond lay out a pretty good blueprint for its return, I think.

The last properly new game in the series came 18 years ago with the Xbox 360's Banjo-Kazooie: Nuts and Bolts, a surprisingly good physics-driven vehicle construction sandbox.

Since then, Banjo and Kazooie showed up as a playable fighter in Super Smash Bros Ultimate. More recently, a fan-made PC port and an Evercade Double Pack have kept the series chugging.

Composer Grant Kirkhope was slightly more hopeful about the prospect of a Banjo-Threeie back in September. "I do know of like three companies that have actually physically pitched to Microsoft or to Rare about making another Banjo-Kazooie game, and I don't think anyone was successful," he said at the time.

#3649. "Game feel is impossible to copy": CEO of Probably Stolen publisher tinyBuild says devs "shouldn't be afraid" of AI clones

GenAI game clones are apparently becoming a real enough threat to the industry that Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick pre-warned "this is likely to invade our business to a greater or lesser extent," while threatening legal action against anyone who naughtily tinkered with GTA VI. More recently, one or more apparent crypto grifters claim to have naughtily tinkered with GTA VI, sparking attempts to vibe-recomp an unoffical PC version. However, contrasting Zelnick's position is tinyBuild CEO Alex Nichiporchik, who quite confidently stated in an interview with Gamesindustry.biz that "devs shouldn't be afraid of it."

Nichiporchik discusses tinyBuild's approach to the gap between announcement and release being important in the age of slop copies (I am trying not to write 'sloppies' into my article, but it is tempting), explaining that "The traditional wisdom previously was to announce early, build up as many wishlists as possible over time, and then you'll have a good basis to launch your game eventually. And that seems to be changing fundamentally." He adds that maintaining a short gap also helps as, to put it simply, "people have short memories, right?" And, unfortunately, he's right; there are so many games coming out that adding something to your wishlist often feels like resigning it to remembering it exists six months later.

He recalls an example of someone making an Android port of Graveyard Keeper, which "barely fit into memory", and was surprised by how "easy" it seemed. But then, he clarifies that the reason it seemed so easy was a lack of care. "There's a reason that every kind of AI slop game feels the same; it's because when you try to make something from zero, AI will multiply your skills, and zero times a thousand is still zero." The people claiming to 'develop' recomps do not care for making a game that feels right, or even one that works; they care only for the short-lived dopamine of being popular on Twitter for fifteen minutes before another slop copy rears its head (and is inevitably revealed to be jankware). Nichiporchik specifies that "game feel is impossible to copy; as long as you have a great game feel and a great game loop, I think you're going to be okay." 'Game feel' is one of the vaguest terms that exists in this field, but I do feel that it refers to something tangible and immediately noticeable when it's gone.

For example, I've recently been replaying the wonderful Celeste, and the 'game feel' of its wavedashing is core to making the practice of blazing through levels so engaging. The wavedash works the same every time, due to precise programming from Extremely OK Games spending time and effort painstakingly ensuring it did in the interest of consistency and unity in movement mechanics. You can't make good art without caring about the quality, even if there are now faster ways to knock together a 'working' game. To borrow an overused but still salient phrase: AI could never.

"This game should probably be capped at 30fps"

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Rockstar's decision to cap GTA 6 at 30fps remains a controversial one, especially after we spent much of the PS5 and Xbox Series X generation getting used to 60fps gameplay on consoles. But if you thought the recent 60fps glitch discovered on Xbox would be a quick piece of salvation, you should probably recalibrate your expectations. As it turns out, it's really more of a 36fps glitch.

That's according to new analysis from Digital Foundry, which has put the supposed 60fps glitch through its paces. On one level, it's true – you can get GTA 6 to run at 60fps. But that's only if you take a plane up into the air, well away from any roving NPCs on the map, and point the camera directly at the sky.

In real gameplay, removing the frame rate cap is still going to leave you with a "mean average" of "about 36 to 37 frames per second," based on testing of the first hour of the game. In other words, "Rockstar isn't keeping anything amazing from you." That's the sort of awkward, variable frame rate that's a lot more unpleasant than a steady 30 frames per second, and DF's analysts agree that "this game should probably be capped at 30fps."

That's not even counting the part where GTA 6 currently runs at an increased speed based on the frame rate, but that's likely just an artifact of the glitch rather than a suggestion that there's some underlying issue with the game. "Ultimately this shouldn't be reflecting on the quality of the code itself," DF's Richard Leadbetter observes. "Obviously there are going to be versions in the future of Grand Theft Auto 6 that will be running at faster than 30fps."

Just don't expect those future versions to run on current-gen consoles. Our first taste of 60fps GTA 6 will likely come on PC, though whether it'll first arrive through an official port or a fan-made PC version remains to be seen.

#3647. "It would end up appealing to no one": The Witcher 4 narrative leads aren't willing to strip away the series' "distinct edge" in the name of chasing a broader audience

In a recent interview with Korean outlet Inven, CD Projekt Red's narrative director Philipp Weber and vice president of story Marcin Blacha shared some words on The Witcher 4, focusing on their awareness that not only will it inevitably be different from The Witcher 3, but also that it needs to be in order to justify its existence. Simultaneously, there's a certain something to The Witcher as a series that they feel is difficult to make tangible, but is something they want to ensure they don't lose sight of.

Weber describes the core of a 'Witcher-like' story to be something that "explores the various facets of human nature — a game for adults", which he clarifies doesn't just mean violence or sex, but "treating the player as a mature adult, asking difficult questions without offering easy answers." While it has been quite a while since its predecessor, they still feel that the upcoming sequel must be true to the series it's part of and earn that numbered title: "If we were to strip away The Witcher's distinct edge just to reach a broader audience, it would end up appealing to no one."

Of course, the biggest change is that of the protagonist, from Geralt to Ciri. Blacha explains that "Ciri isn't calm and composed like Geralt, nor does she hide her emotions easily. She is far more hot-headed and tends to be emotional when making decisions." In terms of how this actually affects the narrative itself and the protagonist's place in it, he elaborates that "when playing as Geralt, players acted more like an arbiter judging how to resolve a situation. When playing as Ciri, you are much more deeply involved in the story through her personal perspective." It's an interesting notion, to state that the difference in role is that where Geralt was more of a fixer, Ciri actually approaches situations on an interpersonal level. Weber seemingly half-jokes that "we find ourselves in a position very similar to Ciri's. Just as Ciri must succeed Geralt, we must create a game that lives up to The Witcher 3."

As for how The Witcher 4 will play, moment to moment, Weber explains that some inspiration has been taken from Cyberpunk 2077 in regards to its open, player-led approach to customisation and, as a result, quests. "You could be a netrunner or a cyber ninja air-dashing into a scene with a double jump. We had to account for all those possibilities available to the player," he recalls. While I can't imagine Ciri will be air-dashing around Kovir, this statement does make me wonder how this approach can be applied to a game with such a specific existing protagonist, rather than the blank slate of Cyberpunk 2077's V. Recalling the side content of The Witcher 3 and its acclaim, he believes that people loved them "because we strived to offer something fresh" and "didn't create quests that merely waste the player's time", which is a principle that "remains unchanged today." Later, he condenses his feelings into the mantra that "A great quest can stem from a compelling story, an engaging character, or fantastic gameplay alone, but overall, there must be harmony."

Towards the end of the interview, Blacha jokes that "One of our greatest achievements is convincing people to finish their workday, buy our game, and then clock into another job as a character inside the game." It's quite a long and engaging read, so if you're invested in The Witcher IV and its narrative development, I do encourage you read the entire thing.

#3646. Deltarune Chapter 6 is playable "from the beginning to the end," Toby Fox says, but the RPG's final part has "only just started"

"Unlike every other chapter, I actually feel like I know what I'm doing this time."

Toby Fox has given eager fans an update on the development of Deltarune Chapter 6 and Chapter 7 - the Undertale follow-up's final two episodes.

"Chapte 6 is progressing well," he wrote in a new blog post. "The game is now a structurally complete draft that can be played from the beginning to the end. All the maps, events, and battles exist. (Although there's still one optional event which is dragging out a bit…)"

While the bones are supposedly all there, Fox explained that he and his team still need to knock out localisation, testing and polishing. "Much of the game looks complete… but, some important scenes and details are still undercooked in their presentation, so it's going to take a bit longer before we can really move to full-on testing."

Deltarune Chapter 6 was previously described as a slightly shorter episode that should hopefully set up the game's finale quite nicely. Despite being on the smaller side, Fox said he understandably doesn't want to rush development and "would like it to be as good as possible."

And since Deltarune's next chapter is almost past the finish line - at least, in some respect - that means certain members of the team have already moved over to Chapter 7.

"Well, we've only just started," Fox continued. "I read out the events and dialogue of Chapter 7 to the team. However, just when the story reached a critical moment, I stopped reading… I told my team they need to complete more of the game before I tell them what happens. Everyone agrees it's more fun this way"

"Unlike every other Chapter, I actually feel like I know what I'm doing this time, so I have a lot of confidence."

Deltarune's been on a long journey to get here, but, thankfully, the end is finally in sight. Deltarune debuted as a free download all the way back in 2018, a second chapter then dropped in 2021, the next two launched together four years later, before the arrival of the most recent Chapter 5 this year.

We don't know exactly how long Deltarune's last two chapters might take, but the good news is that it's already been a pretty fantastic game for years. Here's hoping those loose threads don't dangle for much longer.

#3645. In Defense Of The Legend Of Zelda: Skyward Sword

As I continue to work my way through Ocarina of Time, the same thought keeps bubbling up in my mind like an intrusive thought: I wish I was playing Skyward Sword. Unlike my colleagues, I did not grow up with The Legend of Zelda, coming to the series much later as a professional video game reviewer. It’s from that perspective that I’ve played a lot (though not all) of the big Zelda games and I can’t help but think that Skyward Sword does not deserve the bum rap it typically gets.

That’s a less controversial position to take now that the game has been ported from the Wii to the Nintendo Switch, easing the frustration associated with trying to fight your enemies while navigating the Wii version’s notoriously fussy waggle physics. Combat on the Switch is smoother, with thumb motion taking over for flexing your entire wrist. (If you want the old-school feel, though, you can play with detached Joy-Cons too.) With that upgrade, the directional combat, via which Link can only deal damage to enemies if he hits them at the correct angle, adds a new dimension to what’s been typically a standard sword-and-board affair.

Combat in Skyward Sword feels more like that in a soulslike, not in its difficulty, but in the way it requires a more thoughtful approach than that in most Zelda games. In games before and since Skyward Sword, aside from specific gimmicks like reflecting an octorok’s attack back at it, you’re mostly just flailing and whaling. Skyward Sword forces you to slows you down. You cannot beat an enemy with wild, unconsidered strikes. You must observe the way it defends and break through that defense.

Skyward Sword’s exploration cannot compare to that of Wind Waker or Breath of the Wild. But I think the lack of variety in overworld exploration on your companion bird is made up for by the game’s dungeons, which are some of the series’ best and most unique. I loved shifting forward and backward in time to navigate the Lanayru Mining Facility and the Sandship, and I appreciate how here, the series’ long-present motif of time travel has been shrunk down and made into a discrete game mechanic in a way the series hadn’t really done since Majora’s Mask (another fave of mine).

But honestly, the most enduring qualities of Skyward Sword are the stories and characters. This is the game that let the Groose loose! Groose starts as a petty, meathead bully jealous that Link has Zelda’s attentions. But rather than let that embitter him which, as video game tropes go, might have involved him showing up as a late-game midbossâHi, Seifer from Final Fantasy VIIIâthe feeling empowers him to discover his own destiny, and he winds up lending Link a much-needed helping hand. (Hello again, Seifer from Final Fantasy VIII.) There have been other lovable Zelda side characters who go on their own journeys of self-discovery, but I think Skyward Sword‘s singular focus on one journeyârather than on retelling similar stories split across multiple characters like the champions in BotW, for exampleâmakes Groose stand out that much more.

I also loveÂ this version of Zelda and Linkâthe bold girl and her best friend who are both transformed by their destiny and duties but remain connected due to their sweet and enduring friendship. They are always connected, that’s what the whole series is about. But some versions of them are closer than others, having a dynamic that’s deeper than simply a princess and her knight. Wind Waker had a little bit of that definition. Skyward Sword, though, deepens the relationship between Link and Zelda more effectively.

There’s a beautiful scene between them in which Zelda tearfully apologizes to Link for manipulating his feelings for her to force him to become the hero their world needs. She’s a true princess, taking responsibility for the pain she’s caused Link while acknowledging it needed to be done, and accepting an eternity of slumber as punishment to keep the evil threatening their world at bay. When he rushes toward her to catch her before she seals herself away, almost to say “I don’t care about that, I care about you,” I teared up, moved by how Link was able to convey so much emotion and love for Zelda without saying anything. More than any previous version of the central pair, Skyward Sword‘s Zelda and Link feel like they’re the genesis of the pair we get in Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom, arguably the series’ best versions of them.

Skyward Sword has my whole heart, and I know that makes me rare among Zelda appreciators. But so much of what we’ve come to love about later Zelda games, narratively and mechanicallyâremember, this is the first game that let you skydive and slow your fall with a sailcloth!âyou can see Nintendo experimenting with in Skyward Sword. For that alone, it deserves your reconsideration.

The leads of Leonida, the biggest and best-known effort to recreate GTA 6 on PC, have quit the project, although others are still trying to carry it on.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Just a day after Grand Theft Auto 6 leaker Cyberleek released the executable for the near-complete Xbox build of the game they dropped on Friday, at least two of the leads of Leonida, the biggest and best-known effort to recompile it to run on PC, have called it quits—seemingly under pressure from Take-Two and Rockstar.

The release of the exe made the pirated Xbox build effectively complete, and that opened the door for recomp projects to do their thing—that is, to leverage AI to quickly whip up a version of the game that will run on PC. Some hackers estimated it could be done within a week; Shayder, one of the lead developers on the Leonida project, said on X that followers could "expect a lot of static recompilation work to be done soon."

In a separate message on the Leonida Discord, Shayder tempered expectations a bit, writing that "it will take at least a week" to come up with something playable on PC. During a subsequent livestream, however, the team was seemingly able to get the GTA 6 splash screen to come up on PC, although it crashed after that. It sure seemed like things were moving ahead quickly.

But then things began moving quickly in a different direction. "I quit guys. I’m sorry," NotRexed, apparently the head of the project, posted last night on X. "I really want to make cool stuff but every single time shit happens that I can’t control so I’m stepping away. Thank you everybody, especially in the discord that allowed me to have this opportunity."

Later, they added, "Last post from me. I wanna clear things up. Rockstar taking my server down was only part of the reason. Like I’ve said before, I’m a 15 year old kid. Managing school and sports is hard enough without having middle aged men yell and complain to you on Discord. Goodbye."

In a reply post, NotRexed stated explicitly that "Rockstar shut the server down," and shared an image of the copyright violation notice he'd received from Discord.

Shayder, who had previously predicted rapid progress on the Leonida effort following the release of the Xbox executable, took a more direct approach and simply deleted all of their X posts.

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

This isn't necessarily the end of work to bring GTA 6 (in a probably not-great state) to PC via AI. Other such projects are underway, and there also appears to be an effort to carry on with Leonida: The website remains up, with a new name attached as owner, and there's at least one Discord server dedicated to it, although it appears a little less focused at this point than the original Leonida server. A new Github repository (NotRexed also deleted that) has been set up: It's "a continuation of NotRexed's Leonida project," according to a note on the project, which adds that "development continues here with its full commit history."

The advent of AI greatly simplifies and speeds up the work of bringing console games to PC (as long as you're not too picky about the quality), and that makes life tougher for companies that want to keep a lid on such projects. Still, it's not surprising that Take-Two and Rockstar are going hard on it: In the past, Take-Two has moved aggressively to shut down GTA 5 mod projects, an effort that culminated in its acquisition of the biggest and best of them. I've reached out to Take-Two for more information on the takedown and will update if I receive a reply.

#3643. Modders already have GTA 6 running on PC, after CyberLeek released a full Xbox build of the game

A PC version of Grand Theft Auto 6 - one from unofficial sources, at least - may be closer than we thought. After suddenly returning last week with a near-full build of the Xbox version, notorious leaker CyberLeek has now posted the missing piece they intentionally held back: the game's executable (.exe) file.

"The exe is out. Always free. An early Christmas gift from CL," CyberLeek reportedly wrote, as relayed on Reddit. "The torch passes to the open source re-comp and emulation projects."

Hours later, the recompilation modders and hackers part of the Project Leonida Discord server - the current hub for all GTA 6 recompilation efforts - posted footage of the game booting up on PC.

In just a matter of hours, modders - with the help of Claude AI - managed to turn the leaked Xbox build into a PC port, of sorts. In this Reddit video, you can see the game boot up to the initial setup before hitting a black screen. The build is clearly not yet playable, though Eurogamer has not directly verified those claims.

Shayder, one of the lead developers on Project Leonida, said in a since-deleted post on X that we should "expect a lot of static recompilation work to be done soon." On the project's Discord server, they later clarified that it could take about a week for the build to reach a playable state on PC.

As for CyberLeek, the leaker is still soliciting donations for a secret project "for the gamers", adding in the build's readme file, "Nobody has to give anything, and every release stays free either way. But every donation is a vote for more of this, and so is every trade of the token."

Rockstar has not announced a PC version of GTA 6, but the company has historically released its games on PC several months after their console debut. In October, a report said GTA 6's PC version would arrive in the first quarter of 2027, an unusually short gap between the console and PC releases.

These latest recompilation efforts, however, may force Rockstar to speed up development of the PC version. Though the recompiled build may never reach the level of quality or stability of an official port, many of those eager to play the game on PC likely wouldn't care.

#3642. Ex-Respawn studio Gravity Well announces "hibernation" following previous failure to secure funding and layoffs, but insists "we still believe in the IP and game we were building"

Following a round of layoffs last month that resulted in the loss of 40 jobs, which itself came after a previous source of funding pulled out in the Spring, independent studio Gravity Well has now announced that it is going into "hibernation" for the foreseeable future. The team was largely made up of devs who'd left Titanfall and Apex Legends studio Respawn Entertainment, and under the Gravity Well banner had been working on a new, still-unannounced game for around six years.

A statement posted to the main page on Gravity Well's site reads:

"We don’t exactly know what is next for us or Gravity Well, but we do know we still believe in the IP and game we were building. Even moreso, the team we managed to cultivate was truly world class and we’re going to miss getting to work with them every day. If you’re a hiring manager or recruiter and a Gravity Well resume hits your desk they come with our highest recommendation.

If you’re a publisher or investor and are interested in talking, let's connect!"

The message is signed off by its founders Drew McCoy, Jon 'Slothy' Shiring and Mon Saetern. Besides being the second project led by former Respawn developers to be doomed this year - see also Wildlight's Highguard - it's unfortunately another case of a studio made up of developers with incredible pedigrees being left at the whim of funding accruement in the current state of the industry. That said, it is noteworthy that the team have not shown anything publicly in the six years since their formation, minus a few pieces of concept art which can now be seen on its site. It's still unknown exactly what Gravity Well was working on, but it's likely to have been some kind of movement-based shooter, if the teams' experience on Titanfall, Apex Legends and Call of Duty is anything to go by. Solidarity to all affected, who I hope can find work elsewhere in the industry.

You don't need to know how to code to ask Claude

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

If the race to get GTA 6 running on PC looks like a mess, that's because it is.

Recomp forerunner Leonida and its rapidly expanding Discord community have seemingly been nuked from orbit after developer Rockstar Games decided that's the only way to be sure, but Leonida is just one of many sloppy efforts to convert a leaked Xbox build of GTA 6 into a playable PC version. These projects are universally powered, if not majority-piloted, by AI tools like Claude and Google's Antigravity, which are also behind the recent game recomp boom that even caught Microsoft's attention.

The large community attracted by the unprecedented success and popularity of GTA 6 has made this vibe-coded game explosion clearer than ever. It's also highlighted the glaring difference between the people using AI to expedite programming and the people asking AI to do everything for them.

The Xbox build and executable shared by notorious GTA 6 leaker and crypto grifter Cyberleek chummed the waters. Now, tons of people, some of whom couldn't get a blue square to move around on-screen without AI assistance, are chucking GTA 6 files into AI tools and telling machines to cobble them together. The results have been mixed.

Before the Leonida Discord was taken down, I'd become a regular reader of its feeds and updates. It's hard to overstate just how AI-dependent many contributors in this space are; across the board, would-be GTA 6 porters openly admit to having no technical experience being holding carrots in front of AI agents.

Twitter use Chasm, who's chronicled GTA 6 PC efforts over the past few days, logged just some of the ways that GTA 6 vibe coders interact with AI. "I've gathered some of the prompts I've found from watching dev streams. No this isn't a joke," he says.

We begin with a classic, seemingly fed to Google's Antigravity: "Make no mistakes."

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more

"Keep finding more stuff and working and pushing," implores another promt.

"You need [to do] one thing at a time not a little bit of everything," reads one.

In a Twitter post, former Leonida project lead NotRexed said: "I let Fable 7.2 work overnight with just one prompt: Get GTA 6 running on my PC. I woke up the next morning with the game fully running at 240fps."

Imagine a chef taking a microwave meal out of its cardboard packaging, placing the plastic container on a cold griddle, and then waiting for food to happen, confident that they at least cut steam vents in the cover. These are the people – rather, a non-trivial number of the people – currently trying to get GTA 6 running on PC.

I'm reminded of March comments from Strauss Zelnick, CEO of Rockstar owner Take-Two. Zelnick said the idea of AI making something as complex and high-quality as GTA 6 is "laughable," dismissing the purported ability of gen AI tools replacing creators.

"The notion that somehow new tools would allow an individual to push a button and generate a hit, and market a hit, and bring it to many millions of consumers around the world… It's a laughable notion," he said. You might get a song back if you prompt an AI tool to generate one, he added, but "I defy you to listen to it more than once."

You can't just tell a computer to make GTA 6, Zelnick argued. Yet here we are. Computer, work faster, make no mistakes, and make this game run on PC.

"The community aspect of decompilation has been broken" by a wave of low-effort AI slop, and now a major community tool is shutting down

#3640. Valve push on with their Steam improvements by revamping the Community Market home page and adding a watchlist to it so you're bookmarks will be a lot lighter

Another day, another Steam update! Earlier this year, Valve made some tweaks to Steam's Community Market as part of their ongoing widening of the digital storefront. The maybe Half-Life 3 developer is back with another update for the Community Market, once again bringing some fresh UI/UX bits, as well as some quality of life adjustments that should make it a bit nicer to use.

For starters, there's a new Market home page! "We've rebuilt the Market Home to load faster and present you with the most relevant items from your games," a blog post explains. "Instead of the Popular Items section, which was a small and static slice of millions of items, Trending Items will give you a glimpse into what’s new in the games you’re currently playing. The game links move up to the top spot and are now personalized, so rather than a flat and unchanging list, you get quick access to the items you're most likely to be interested in."

Next up in the update is the addition of a watchlist feature. Before, if you wanted to follow a number of items in the marketplace you'd need to bookmark everything, but now you can just save things to your watchlist; this includes the likes of specific listings, particular item types with any filters you've applied, and even specific searches, again with filters and search text. You can also apply custom names to watchlist entries in case two of them end up looking particularly similar.

There were a few other smaller bits to this update too. You'll find a new section that highlights Steam community items, i.e. trading cards and emotes, from games you've played. If you have anything listed on the marketplace, you can now change the price without having to relist it. There's a list view option while browsing items. And market pages now load faster and are more responsive. A convenient sounding update for the Steam Community Market connoisseur! Which is already live, by the way.

#3639. Microsoft reportedly looked into killing paid multiplayer for next-gen Xbox Helix consoles

A new report from Windows Central details how Xbox was reportedly looking into removing the paywall that prevents players without Xbox Live from playing online games, only to potentially renege on its decision sometime during production of the next-gen device.

"Sources close to Microsoft's plans tell me Xbox Helix was originally conceived as a true console-PC hybrid with access to Windows PC games and stores such as Steam, alongside another major change: no paywall for online multiplayer," says the Windows Central report. It goes on to note that this Xbox Live-free plan was iterated upon under Xbox's previous leadership, but with Asha Sharma's appointment as Xbox head in February, all that apparently changed. I guess she did promise "radically different business models", after all.

The revised plan has reportedly been altered thanks to a myriad of factors affecting the Xbox business: new management, rising component costs, and a shifting hardware strategy, are all outlined specifically in the report. We've previously heard that Xbox's next-gen console could cost up to $1,800, with a handheld version coming in 2027 and a full release by holiday 2028 (a Helix console at $1,200 would mean a 50 percent increase on top of Series X's current price, for what it's worth). Sharma has stressed Helix will launch as "a family of devices" that will act as a bridge between PC and Xbox capable of playing games from both platforms.

If Xbox has, indeed, decided to scrap the idea of free online multiplayer access, it'll be a blow to the idealistic 'PC and Xbox' platform that Microsoft has been touting for the past few years: PC players do not need a subscription in order to access online modes, so - right out the gate - there will be a division between one group of players and the other. Perhaps this is why we've heard a little change in the tone of how Sharma and other Xbox bosses are talking about Helix more recently - these hints that the console will be a true PC-and-console hybrid have died down, and been replaced by insinuations that we'll see more of a traditional console with the "ability to play your PC games."

Xbox has been running Xbox Live as a service since 2002, when it launched on the original Xbox console. By 2005, it was split into gold and silver tiers to distinguish free players from those that paid. In 2023, the service was fully renamed Xbox Game Pass Core, looping in access to the base roster of Game Pass games with online play.

Gravity Well, founded in 2020 as an "anti-crunch" game studio, lost its funding earlier this year and wasn't able to find a new backer.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Gravity Well, an "anti-crunch" studio founded in 2020 by former Apex Legends executive producer Drew McCoy and lead software engineer Jon Shiring, is entering "hibernation" after losing funding for its game.

Gravity Well's launch in 2020 came with high hopes. Founded by veterans of Call of Duty, Titanfall, and Apex Legends, it made the health of the team "an absolute top priority," McCoy said at the time.

"That means we are anti-crunch. That means good compensation. That means everyone at Gravity Well has creative freedom, because when someone else makes all of the decisions, work isn't fun and the end product isn't as good."

But like so many other ambitious new studios launched around that time, it fell victim to the post-pandemic retrenchment and has effectively shuttered without releasing a game. The shutdown comes just a month after the studio laid off more than 40 people in what it said was a "fight for survival" caused by the loss of funding. It also warned that "given the current state of the industry our future is uncertain."

A message now posted on the Gravity Well website (via RPS) says the funding situation hasn't changed, and "sadly the time has come for Gravity Well to go into hibernation."

"We don’t exactly know what is next for us or Gravity Well, but we do know we still believe in the IP and game we were building," the message states. "Even moreso, the team we managed to cultivate was truly world class and we're going to miss getting to work with them every day. If you're a hiring manager or recruiter and a Gravity Well resume hits your desk they come with our highest recommendation."

The announcement concludes with an invitation to publishers and investors to reach out if they're interested in supporting the project.

#3637. "That philosophy has not changed for us because of GTA 6": CD Projekt Red are staying the course on The Witcher 4 and Cyberpunk 2 after Rockstar's smash success

"We have certain ambitions when it comes to [The Witcher 4 and] Cyberpunk 2"

For publicly traded game developers, there is surely one question, with all manner of variations, that will surely be coming up again and again over the next few months: what impact will GTA 6 have on your games? CD Projekt Red were subjected to such questioning in their latest earnings call, part of which was related to sales figures of The Witcher 3 and Cyberpunk 2077, that boring kind of thing. But CEO Michal Nowakowski did also respond to a comment about how GTA 6 may affect the development of The Witcher 4 and Cyberpunk 2.

"We have certain ambitions when it comes to [The Witcher 4 and] Cyberpunk 2, they have not changed when it comes to GTA 6," Nowakowski quite plainly explains in response to a question about how the biggest game of the year may influence budget or design, already sounding just that little bit exasperated over the questions related to Rockstar's latest. "If anything happened as a result of GTA 6, it's always great to see games like that because they show you how much cool stuff can be done. That's for sure an inspiration in many ways for our developers. In terms of the budget, I gave a response [in an interview at] Gamescom; games The Witcher or Cyberpunk 2, although they are not GTA, are not budget-driven developments."

Nowakowski goes on to clarify that he doesn't mean this in the sense of not caring about budgets, or that they have infinite money, but noted that you "cannot make games," with solely that focus. "They are ambition-driven developments and money is important, the budgets are not indefinite, that's not what we're saying. And honestly, that philosophy has not changed for us because of GTA 6." This is obviously kind of a non-answer in one sense, but I think it does point to how GTA 6 is going to create some uncomfortable expectations for many triple-A devs when next to none of them will have Rockstar money to fulfill them.

In any case, obviously the next big thing for CD Projekt Red is The Witcher 3's Songs of the Past expansion. Still no release date attached to that one, though it's currently expected to release sometime in 2027 next year. The Witcher 4 is then slated for release not long after that in 2028, but in this day and age, I'm sure a delay would be an incredibly safe bet to make.

Obviously, you need to steal cars in Grand Theft Auto 6; itâs in the name of the game. But you might as well get something out of it beyond just new wheels and some money, so how about scoring a trophy along the way?

The Bravado Banshee is a nice ride that you get a mission to steal in GTA 6âs third chapter, via a character named Randy. You could luck out and find a Banshee on the street, but if you want the Capital Offense trophy, you can kill two birds with one stone by hitting up the Sunrise Premium Autos showroom in Southside. Youâll find it between Vice City International Airport and Peacock Bay, next to an Illegals Good Store.

Note that you canât do this before you do Randyâs mission âCloninâ Keys, Makinâ Gs.â Why? The Bravado Banshee, like a lot of expensive cars in the game, requires a key cloner, and Randy is the person who gives you one as part of that mission. After he’s added the app to your phone, you can head to Sunrise Premium Autos and walk back to the showroom where a shiny blue Bravado Banshee is just sitting there.

Clone the key via the same method you would use to slim-jim a car door, and then step on in. The next part is how you get the Capital Offense trophy: Drive the car straight through the glass window and then gun it before the police get there. The trophy should pop immediately.

The trophy itself is a reference to the easiest and most reliable way to get a Banshee in Grand Theft Auto 3, where you would just visit a car showroom in the south part of the map, sit in a Banshee in the showroom, and then drive it through the glass window. Regardless of what you choose, youâre a bit richer and a bit further along in your progress toward a platinum trophy or a mythic achievement. Not bad for an afternoonâs work.

Legacy Uniques, World Boss Diablo summons, and even Moophisto are carrying over into Diablo 4 season 16

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Blizzard scored a major win with Diablo 4's nostalgic season 15, which coincided perfectly with the series' 30th anniversary and the triumphant return of BlizzCon, not to mention the announcement of Diablo 5. Season of Hell's Legacy pulled many of its headlining features from Diablo 1, 2, and 3, including a questline recreation of the first game's main storyline. The season has been a hit with players, so it made sense when Blizzard confirmed that some of its features would stay in the game permanently. Now, we know which features exactly, and it's clear Blizzard is doubling down on the nostalgia.

"We heard overwhelming requests for features from Season of Hell’s Legacy to carry forward as permanent game features," reads Blizzard's announcement of Diablo 4 season 16, now officially titled Season of Tyrael's Gambit. "While the entire season couldn’t come along for the ride, we are implementing the following features with the launch of Season of Tyrael's Gambit that will carry forward in both Eternal and Seasonal realms:"

By far my favorite addition in season 15 was the beautifully reimagined Old Tristram, and that'll remain accessible, along with its side quests and Deckard Cain's books, via the portal in the Imperial Library. Real ones will know about Cow Island, a callback to one of the series' most beloved Easter eggs, and that will also remain accessible along with the Moophisto world boss summon. Likewise, the big Uber Diablo World Boss summon is coming along for the ride in season 16, as well as the Annihilus Seal he drops. And speaking of items, the Legacy Uniques from older Diablo games are sticking around, as is the Hellfire Torch Charm, a nod to Diablo 2.

Arguably the most notable season 15 feature getting stamped into the game permanently is the Prime Evil Council fight, which puts you up against Diablo, Mephisto, and Baal simultaneously. Blizzard says that battle will work like a typical Lair Boss in terms of summoning and claiming rewards, and that you won't need any materials to access the encounter. All players in the battle will need their own Wirt's Lucky Coin to get into the Council's Hoard chest and reap the rewards.

Meanwhile, season 15's Capstone Dungeons will be available in Torment 10+, with all spawns being tuned to their equivalents in Torment 13. Blizzard says "these will be the best source for earning Prime Evil Splinters," which are what you need to get those sweet Prime Evil powers. Speaking of sweet, season 15's Waking Nightmares dungeons, which are normal-size dungeons inspired by iconic moments from previous Diablo games, are being made permanent, but only through Chronicle of Nightmares dungeon keys and not in the overworld. Finally, head to the Pit for a chance to fight "monster families from previous Diablo games."

Diablo 4 season 16, kicking off December 1, is all about the evolving threat posed by the Úllo Sar death cult, which is exciting enough, but it'll be really hard to top season 15 for me as a fan of the series from the beginning. Luckily, Blizzard has confirmed I'll be able to go back to Old Tristram and read Deckard Cain's journals any time I please. I think I'll stay a while.

Diablo 5 is Blizzard's darkest ARPG yet, and that's the best way to honor the game that changed my life 30 years ago

#3633. Bare fist, megastructure climbing roguelike White Knuckle gets its penultimate region in The Core, a sterile, hostile reactor sector that you'll probably die in

Hope you've been training your grip strength

The beauty of stepping into a digital world is that it allows me to accomplish things I couldn't possibly dream of doing in the real one, like, say, climbing anything that's higher than your average step ladder. White Knuckle is one such game that's all about playing around with uncomfortable heights, and a new update for the early access roguelike went live this week introducing a new, hostile environment: The Core.

The sixth region to be added to the game, and the "penultimate challenge," implying that there's just one more area to come after this one, The Core takes you to Habitation Blue's reactor sector. "Use everything you have available to fight through the now Mass-controlled Superstructure Automated Processing System (SAPS) and her array of mechanized defenses," explains a Steam news post. "The Core is the sterile power station of the Superstructure, a massive network of coolant lines, offices, catwalks, and more, all of which is highly secured by an army of turrets, drones, and androids. Even without the Mass hot on your tail it would not be easy to escape."

There are a few new subregions to be found too, of course, but more importantly a new major artifact. It's called The Scissors, and with it you cut off your hands ("yes, really") to "gain a spectral form that increases your reach, hand stamina, and damage," while using the artifact. You can also throw the scissors like a boomerang to hurt enemies from afar, and "killing enemies also counts as eating if using Survival Mode binding, or the perks Conditioned Polyphagia & Unstoppable Conviction."

Beyond this there's a selection of new weapons, like the piton crossbow which shoots "pitons at range, to set up routes and to deal extreme damage." The pulse pump is a new trinket that introduces a chargeable mid-air jump. There's new perks like one called nest egg, where you gain a "second major artifact at the start of the Nest, at the cost of halving all roach deposits in your run." Previous regions have also received some new room tiles, and there's a few fresh cosmetics to pick up too. There's some secret thing to find in this update as well, "but you'll need to play to find out…" Hop to it, I guess!

#3632. Atari Homebrew Awards Canceled Over Torrent Of AI Games: ‘I Saw No Path Forward’

Another awards ceremony is struggling with how to handle an influx of genAI games. The Atari Homebrew Awards is in its ninth year, or at least it was going to be. It’s been canceled after its organizer hit an impasse with how to handle submissions that might have been made with AI.

“Keeping up with the large number of AI assisted game development had become increasingly difficult as this year wore on with some developers even releasing multiple games a week with the aid of AI,” ZeroPage Homebrew wrote on the Atari Age forum (via Time Extension). “This flood of new AI games forced me reevaluate the way games were qualified and judged for the upcoming AHAs.”

The task for ZeroPage wasn’t simply going through all of the submissions; it was figuring out what cutoff, if any, to have for AI use. Allowing games that were 100-percent generated by AI was out of the question, but what about games that used AI for music, art, or coding? How much of the game could be made by AI before it went against the purpose of the whole awards ceremony?

Linked below an important announcement you should probably read. Please keep in mind this won't change the ZPH stream and we will keep playing all the awesome games made by the community!https://t.co/0odTADzfh9

— ZeroPage Homebrew (@zeropagehomebre) November 23, 2026

On top of that, there are no easy ways to vet the amount of AI used to make games. It requires that people honestly disclose it, leading to a grey area in which community reactions can lead to witch hunts and testing software can lead to false positives.

“We were always able to come up with a solution for small issues in previous years but the advent of AI marked a seismic shift in the way retro games were being made,” ZeroPage wrote. “I saw no path forward and made the difficult decision to suspend the Atari Homebrew Awards this year.”

The forum post now has hundreds of comments as users react to the news and debate AI’s place in the Atari homebrew scene and beyond. “Most people who use AI are tools. (derogatory),” one person wrote. Another said a “tool” was exactly what AI turned a work colleague of theirs into. “[He] told us how when he woke up in the middle of the night to go to the bathroom he would check if there was any pending question so he could unblock the AI agent,” the person wrote. “He also confessed he started to dread looking at his phone because answering would take 15-20 mins…his sleep patterns were going the way of the dodo.”

One of the cars Randy wants in GTA 6 is the Ocelot Bloodless Jugular—and don't let the name fool you, its a slick and speedy ride that'll you'll be tempted to keep for yourself.

But Randy doesn't know the locations of many of the cars on his wishlist, and can't point you to the Ocelot Bloodless Jugular: you just need to keep an eye out for it. Luckily, we spotted it ourselves, so just follow the simple steps below to find it.

Head to Belville: It's a town in Leonard County, in the central eastern part of the map, a bit south of Lake Leonida and north of La Perle.

In the northern edge of Belville there's a little cluster of four homes laid out almost in an X pattern. The southernmost home of that cluster has a garage you can break into. Once you open the garage door, you'll see the white Ocelot Bloodless Jugular.

You'll need the key cloner to get in, which I assume you already have since you're doing jobs for Randy. No need to worry about the tracker, it's a standard one so it won't transmit your location to the cops. You still don't want to dawdle, because the owner of the car has a gun and he's not afraid to use it. He'll start shooting if he sees you boost the car.

Randy will pay you $10,615 for the Ocelot Bloodless Jugular. He'll pay an extra $5,000 if you bring it to him in pristine condition.

#3630. Bitmap Brothers' iconic, robotic RTS game Z is unofficially back thanks to an open source, 3D remake

There can be such a wonderful charm that comes from fan games because the people that make them really are just in it for the love of the (literal) game. They ain't gonna make any money from this thing! So I'm quite tickled by OpenZ, a 3D remake of the 1996 RTS game Z from The Bitmap Brothers that's completely open source (and, thankfully, hand made).

As it currently stands, OpenZ is a one-person operation who's remaking the game to celebrate its 30th anniversary. "This is the faithful 3D remake we always wanted but never got. Every single detail has been meticulously recreated and restored with an almost ridiculous level of attention," explains the game's itch.io page. "OpenZ is completely free and open source. It will never be sold: no donations, no commercial use, ever. All assets are 100% original, and no copyrighted material from the original game is used."

At the moment there's only two levels, though it's sounding like it's the full run of them, described as having been "meticulously restored and polished to an extreme level of detail," with some added improvements thanks to "30 years of RTS game design experience." There's a few new bits to find in this remake too, like new mech and electrobot units.

It sounds like there are bigger plans for the remake overall, presumably for the full game too: "This is only the beginning. Together as a community we can bring Z back to its former glory: more restored classic levels, completely original new levels, new units and maybe even multiplayer." As mentioned, it's completely free to download and play too, so where's the harm in giving it a go!

Chris Evans says Marvel bosses Kevin Feige and Lou D’Esposito pitched him a Nomad movie prior to Avengers: Doomsday.

"They said, ‘We’d love to continue making movies with you. Steve would no longer be Captain America; he would be Nomad," Evans told Entertainment Weekly. "They sent me a pitch and it was a great pitch. It really was. But for whatever reason at the time, I was very happy with how things wrapped up. It didn’t feel like it was the thing I was looking to do at the time."

Steve Rogers took on the persona of Nomad in Captain America #180, having given up the Cap mantle after becoming disillusioned with the United States government. Taking the name Nomad because felt like a "man without a country," Steve still defended the innocent from the evils of the world at large... but as more of a vigilante. Think Hawkeye becoming a mask-wearing, street-level vigilante known the Ronin after the Blip. Steve would become Cap again in Captain America #184, however.

How is Steve Rogers even in Avengers: Doomsday, you might ask? Well, all we really know is that it definitely has to do with Loki. In one of the Avengers: Endgame Encore post-credits scenes, he appears at Steve and Peggy's door and tells them he's there to help.

Avengers: Doomsday arrives in US theaters on December 18 and a few days earlier in the UK on December 16. For more on the MCU, check out our guide to the Marvel timeline and how to watch the Marvel movies in order.

#3628. More than 39 million people have played GTA 6 on PlayStation alone, Sony says, as the game breaks all-time player numbers on the platform

Sony's revealed staggering statistics relating to the popularity of Grand Theft Auto on PlayStation 5, not least that more than 39 million unique people have played the game there. That's more than the official GTA 6 day-one sales tally of 32.5m copies across all platforms.

Unsurprisingly, with such massive numbers, GTA 6 is a record-breaker on PlayStation. According to the PlayStation Blog, the game has recorded the highest number of concurrent players on PlayStation ever, surpassing any previous record across all kinds of game - multiplayer, free-to-play and single-player.

In addition, PlayStation also saw "the largest number of newly connected PS5 consoles on a single day" since the console's launch, outside of end-of-year holidays, suggesting that Rockstar's latest game, more than any other PS5 game released so far, has driven hardware sales. GTA 6 is apparently the first game played on 70 percent of new PS5 consoles.

The average GTA 6 playtime, per person, is a considerable 17.4 hours, the blog says, and the total number of hours spent playing the game is 683 million - a number so high I can't contextualise it.

Microsoft hasn't announced equivalent data for Xbox but I assume the game is a record-breaker there, too, given that it broke pre-order Xbox Store records in the same way GTA 6 did on PlayStation. However, GTA 6 is estimated to have sold far more copies on PlayStation - as many as 75 percent of its total sales, according to Alinea Analytics analyst Rhys Elliott.

Elliott estimated that GTA 6 amassed a colossal 44.9m sales by the end of its opening weekend, and that 33.7m of those were on PlayStation 5 (which still doesn't reach the '39 million unique players' stat Sony has just trotted out) and 11.2m were on Xbox. That amount of sales would earn Rockstar something like $4bn in revenue.

The arrival of GTA 6 has, then, been seismic. The game has wowed critics and dominated conversation not only in the games industry but also across entertainment news and mainstream news. Meanwhile, however, we await the verdict in the Rockstar Games employment tribunal in Scotland, relating to the sudden firing of 34 employees a year ago. Was Rockstar union-busting, as alleged? It'll be a historic ruling if deemed so.

#3627. I'm not smart enough for the blocky, Factorio-esque spaceship and -station building sim Astario, but now that it's out in early access maybe you could be

There are many different kinds of smarts, and the kind of smarts I am are absolutely zero help when it comes to games like Astario, a spaceship and space station building factory sim reminiscent of Factorio that just launched into early access. I think there's just so many moving parts in ways I can't wrap my head around, but I'm fairly confident that some of you will be, so I'll try to use the smarts I do have to tell you about it a bit more.

Astario puts you in a spaceship in, uh, space, and oh what a big space it is. I have no idea if it's a to scale universe or anything, but it certainly looks quite expansive. There is a Minecraftian quality to it in that you must fly about and find resources from things like asteroids and other bits of technological scrap, all of which is divided up into blocks. You can get quite granular with it, inspecting each individual cube up close to see if it's a material that you can make use of, adding it to your haul for use elsewhere.

As you acquire different kinds of blocks, be they functional or structural, you can build up various new vehicles and "create an imposing machine where all components work together to achieve your goal. Plan or design your build out of armor blocks, power supplies, life support components, tools, and production machinery. Construct an orbital station with a stash of cargo containers, or anchor your production base to an asteroid and turn its ores into more blocks, fully automatically. Equip your ship with docking ports for refueling or recharging." How you build things is up to you, you've seemingly got a lot of free reign in terms of artistic expression.

And then of course there's bits of production machinery you can produce that in turn net you recipes and the like so you can continue to improve your ship or space stations. "All production blocks have input and output ports that can be automated using logistic pipes which use request-based item routing," explains the game's Steam page of how techy you can get with it. "Simply hook up your inputs to a cargo container, and the machine will pull what it needs. Mining can be temporarily automated using specialized drills, which mine until the resources within its scope are depleted." If any of this sounds like it's up your alley, then you can pick up Astario on Steam in early access now.

#3625. GTA 6 players are already starting to get very good at heists, despite all the new challenges Rockstar has added to the game

Grand Theft Auto 6 has been out for a little while now, and already players are showing off their skills when it comes to the game's many heists. Despite the challenges in getting away clean, some are proving it's possible.

For one, sneaking into a bank while the vault is open and stuffing your bags full of marked bills is a tricky process of gradually making your way through rooms and taking out guards as quietly as possible. While the police in the clip below were called to an eventual breakout of violence, a lengthy getaway allowed for a cheeky payday of almost $100,000 in cash.

This crew really cracked a whole bank vault and walked out with almost $100K in GTA 6 💰🏦🚔😮‍💨 #gtavi #gta pic.twitter.com/pJyFXREBvY

One especially impressive element of Grand Theft Auto 6 is how many of its little mechanics interact with each other. As you can see below, if you bring a vehicle with a winch to a cash machine, you can actually pull it off the wall and drag it away from the scene of the crime.

Why rob a bank in GTA 6 when you can just take the whole ATM💸 How to do it❓- Hook the ATM up to a vehicle with a winch- Drag it through the streets until the cash cases fall out- Shoot them open and get out fast, the cops come quickly!(via u/MelloYello917) pic.twitter.com/5eXbULJWP3

As you progress through Grand Theft Auto 6, the game actually introduces you to both styles of heists. Without spoiling exactly how this happens, you're told how to go about taking on such criminal ventures, and you can continue to do so throughout the game at your pleasure. Still, even after you've been tutorialised, pulling off one of these heists is no joke, and can easily turn chaotic.

This GTA 6 robbery sequence was CRAZY, I couldn't even think straight . pic.twitter.com/l65xSFRoSr

Here's a little tip for those of you looking to pull off a heist yourself. You're told that safety deposit boxes can be rifled through for additional loot. However, when you actually make your way into a vault, these will be closed without much sign on which you can access. If you use the focus mode (by pushing in both L3 and R3), it will highlight boxes which you can shoot open. This, of course, may garner unwanted attention, so whether or not you think it's worth doing is part of the risk/reward dilemma you'll have to reckon with. As is the case with so much stuff in GTA 6 including, but not limited to, car-jacking.

There are tons of unique and collectible weapons in GTA 6 but these are the best and easiest to snap up early in the game.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

GTA 6 has a ton of unique weapon variants all with their own names and mods. They're all special custom builds of stock guns and weapons with unique skins, but some of them are way more worth the trouble to hunt down than others. You'll find some of them easily—every Ammu-Nation has a unique gun sitting out for you to buy. The best unique weapons are a little more hidden. There are treasure hunts and easter eggs and a whole lot that you'll grab by fighting your way through a gang hideout.

The Assassin Nipper is at the south tip of the eastern island in the Permit Keys.

Use Focus Mode to find the hidden cache for the Assassin Nipper .38

This is the easiest unique weapon to grab right at the start of the game and totally worth the boat ride to grab it. There isn't even any combat to get to it, like many of these other uniques. The Assassin Nipper comes with a suppressor attachment, which is a really expensive mod to buy early in the game. Pick it up as soon as you've got free range in Key Lento from an old shipwreck in the Permit Keys near the military base location.

Another great Chapter 1 snag is this sniper rifle at a Kingfisher hideout. The combat to get it is minimal (don't get between that tiger and its prey) so it's easy to pick up early. It's a bolt action that can't equip a silencer, so it isn't exactly a stealth tool, but it can help Jason pick off gangsters in a hideout before even going inside. It comes with a stock and a basic dot sight.

A variant of the Vom Feur V5FC, found in Port Gellhorn at a Kolt gang hideout. It's up on the top floor of the motel by the La Cascara Motel safe, so you pretty much have to complete this illegal operation to grab it. I recommend coming up the south stairwell that's less guarded and hugging the outer walkways to get most of the way to the loot room by stealth. It's worth it though. The Scrapper is a silenced longarm SMG fairly early in the game with an extended mag and a flashy paint job.

This Duke Carbine variant doesn't have a suppressor but it is quite high accuracy for a full auto assault rifle with a heavy stock and 7" pistol barrel mod. The Kolt 556 is easier to smash and grab than the Scrapper, though. You've got to fight in and out of the Kolt stash house, but it's a small joint so it's not too hard to get away clean. It's in a gun case on a kitchen table near the safe full of pills.
